validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all confirmed clean. Permian Katy Pipeline (P2K) is a real proposed intrastate gas pipeline: Sempra Energy (via Sempra LNG & Midstream) and Boardwalk Pipeline Partners LP jointly launched a non-binding open season on it in Aug 2017 (Natural Gas Intelligence, 2017-08-14), it received an initial Railroad Commission of Texas permit in Apr 2018 covering 17 named counties (Marrs Ellis & Hodge LLP eminent-domain blog, texascondemnationprojects.com, 2018-05-31), it appears in Pipeline & Gas Journal's Oct-2018 'Planned Pipelines' industry roundup with full specs, was still listed among several Permian-to-Gulf pipelines that had NOT reached FID as of Sep 2019 (Midland Reporter-Telegram, 2019-09-16), and is carried in EIA's own Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (Historical Projects tab) as 'Permian to Katy Pipeline' / Sempra, Boardwalk Energy / Status=Cancelled, last updated 2020-06-12. Four independent origins (trade press, a Texas eminent-domain law firm, a regional newspaper, and the federal EIA dataset), none tracing to GEM. Correctly classified as a proposed natural gas transmission line moving Permian Basin gas to the Gulf Coast/Mexico market -- FuelSource='Permian Basin' and Fuel='Gas' both confirmed. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 45-row roster: no match -- P0314 is NOT the same project as any other row here. Note for future researchers: several LATER, unrelated Waha-to-Katy corridor pipelines exist in EIA's dataset under similar route descriptions -- Matterhorn Express (WhiteWater Midstream, in service 2024), Trident Intrastate (Kinder Morgan, under construction), Traverse (WPC JV/Targa), Mustang Express (Arm Energy) and Hugh Brinson/Warrior (Energy Transfer) -- all built or sanctioned years after P2K was shelved, with completely different sponsors; none of them are in this 45-row roster and none should ever be confused with or merged into P0314.

validity.recommendation: Consider recording Owner1 as the actual joint-venture party 'Boardwalk Pipeline Partners LP' (with Loews Corp noted as its ultimate parent) rather than 'Loews Corp' itself -- every independent source names Boardwalk directly and none names Loews.
validity.researcher_notes: Owner2='Sempra Energy' 50% is directly confirmed -- NGI's opening sentence names 'Sempra Energy and Boardwalk Pipeline Partners LP' as the two joint-venture sponsors verbatim. But Owner1='Loews Corp' 50% is one level removed from what any source actually says: NGI, the PGJ planned-pipelines listing, and the Texas eminent-domain blog all name 'Boardwalk Pipeline Partners LP' (PGJ: 'Owner 2: Boardwalk Pipeline Partners LP, 50%') as the 50% partner, never 'Loews Corp'. Loews Corp is Boardwalk's ultimate/majority parent (well known publicly since Loews's 2018 buyout of Boardwalk's public unitholders) but that parent relationship doesn't appear in any of the four documents I read for this project specifically, so I can't cite a source for the parent-subsidiary link itself. This is a naming-precision question, not a factual error -- the substance (a 50/50 JV between the Sempra family and the Boardwalk/Loews family) is right either way -- so flagged as caveat, not a hard concern. Not changing the value myself since GEM's own convention elsewhere in this roster (e.g. Black Bear Transmission LLC vs its parent Project Tarpon Holdco LLC) sometimes lists the operating subsidiary and sometimes the parent, so this may be deliberate.
